ORB.paraphrase: For a fibration f:(X,Delta)->Y from a compact Fujiki-class-C manifold with rational SNC boundary (coefficients in [0,1], including 1) onto a normal compact space, the log Kodaira dimension of the total pair is at least that of a very general fiber plus Campana's orbifold-base invariant kappa(f|Delta). Corollaries: log subadditivity (Cor 6.2), ordinary C_{n,m} over any alg. closed char-0 field, core corollaries.

ORD.paraphrase: Iitaka's C_{n,m} for every surjective projective connected-fibre morphism of smooth projective varieties over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0 (F = geometric generic fibre). Main new input: Projective adjoint positivity (ORD:01-introduction.tex:82-104).

VAR.paraphrase: For projective connected-fibre surjections of smooth quasi-projective varieties with log-Kodaira-nonnegative base; Var = transcendence degree of the minimal field of birational definition of the whole geometric generic fibre. Claims Popa's Conjecture 3.8 and (Cor 1.2) Viehweg's C+_{n,m} in all dimensions.

BSA.paraphrase: For f:Y->X between compact Kahler manifolds with K_Y+Delta ~_Q f^*L, Delta effective SNC with coefficients in [0,1], the moduli b-line bundle (log-canonical-threshold discriminant) descends on some compact Kahler model S and a multiple is globally generated; no projectivity.

main_statement.latex: \kappa(X,L_X)\leq\kappa(Y,L_Y)+\kappa(F,L_F).\ \text{If either term on the right is }-\infty,\text{ then }H^0(X,mL_X)=0\text{ for every }m>0.  \quad \kappa(X,K_X+E)=\kappa(Y,K_Y+D)+\kappa(F,K_F+E_F).
main_statement.paraphrase: Formalized manuscript (REV): f:(X,E)->(Y,D) surjective connected-fibre morphism of smooth projective reduced-SNC pairs over C with Supp f^*D in Supp E, X and every boundary stratum smooth over V=Y\Supp D; F very general fiber. Then the reverse (upper) log Kodaira inequality holds, with vanishing of all log plurigenera if base or fiber has kappa=-infinity; with ORB's Cor 6.2 this gives Popa's logarithmic additivity in the stratum-smooth projective formulation.

comparator.statement: For f : StratumSmoothFibration X Y E D: VeryGenerally Y (fun y => y.point in D.complement and for all F : FiberModel f y, F.boundary.kodaira = bot -> E.kodaira = D.kodaira + F.boundary.kodaira and every s in E.sections m (m>0) is 0).
comparator.model: SmoothProjectiveVariety = integral C-scheme, smooth of fixed relative dimension, closed immersion into Proj of MvPolynomial (Fin (N+1)) C; ReducedSNCBoundary = finitely many Cartier ideal sheaves with all nonempty intersections empty or smooth of the right codimension; log pluriforms = elements s of the m-th tensor power of the top exterior power of Kaehler differentials of the function field with t^m s in the regular lattice on every affine where the boundary ideal is principal (t); kodaira = sup of k such that some degree-m nonzero section s has k algebraically independent rational functions r_i with r_i s still sections (bot if none); VeryGenerally = outside countably many proper closed subsets; FiberModel = a SmoothProjectiveVariety with pullback square onto the fiber and a reduced SNC boundary whose ideal is the comap of E's.

main_statement.match_check: Faithful to the paper's NEGATIVE-FIBER BRANCH only (REV:sections/reduction.tex:61-66): kappa(F,L_F)=-inf => H^0(X,mL_X)=0 for all m>0, hence kappa(X,L_X)=kappa(Y,L_Y)+(-inf). Definitions checked: kodaira via algebraically independent section ratios equals Iitaka dimension (max transcendence degree of ratio fields in one degree); log-pluriform condition imposed on principal affines covers X because union_cartier holds; StratumSmoothFibration encodes surjectivity, connected closed fibers, f^{-1}(Supp D) in Supp E, smoothness of f and of every nonempty boundary stratum over Y\D. In WithBot ENat, a + bot = bot, so the first conjunct is just E.kodaira = bot. Minor weakening: the comparator quantifies over FiberModels without asserting one exists (ReverseInequalityStatement in Basic.lean:423 does include Nonempty). The Lean proof is actually stronger than needed (nonvanishing on a nonempty Zariski open, FiberNegative.lean:33-49).
main_statement.formalized_vs_claimed: Formalized: the trivial branch (a 5-line restriction-plus-adjunction argument in the paper). NOT formalized: the finite case kappa(X)<=kappa(Y)+kappa(F), the negative-BASE vanishing (the real content: a log Popa-Schnell base-nonvanishing statement), the section-construction proposition, all Hodge theory, the additivity corollary, and everything in ORB/VAR/ORD/BSA. Basic.lean:423-454 states ReverseInequalityStatement / LogarithmicSubadditivityStatement / LogarithmicAdditivityStatement / MainTheoremStatement and Descent.lean:52 states SectionConstructionStatement as Prop definitions only (no proofs). RootFactor.lean + Descent.lean + Blowup.lean prove the algebraic core of the paper's zero test (REV Lemma 3.3) but are outside the target DAG.
main_statement.note_for_comparator: lean/docs/033.md says so explicitly: 'The finite-dimension and negative-base branches of the paper's additivity theorem are outside this selected statement.' A successful compile certifies only the easy direction; it lends no support to Iitaka C_{n,m}, Campana's conjecture or Popa's conjectures.

eureka_candidates.item: O04+O06 / P01+P04 / R14+R16: adjoint positivity of the highest Hodge line (K_S+jL big on the full-period quotient S, M=p^*L at original level), via strict rank loss of the line on every boundary and finite-ramification divisor

eureka_candidates.for: It is the single new input that turns the classical reduction (relative Iitaka fibration + canonical bundle formula + Viehweg weak positivity + KP/Hashizume addition) into a full proof of C_{n,m}; Birkar (2009) identifies the kappa(F)=0 case as exactly the obstruction. L contains: M nef (Kawamata/Ambro/FG), M b-nef and abundant only after generically finite base change (Ambro 2005, which breaks K_W and effectivity), K_S+D big on period images (BC), algebraicity (BBT). None states that the nef line itself absorbs the boundary and ramification (nu(L|E) < nu(L)) so that K_S+jL is big. Statement is short and checkable (elliptic modular curve: deg lambda = 1/12, K+j lambda big for j>24). Reused in four of the five manuscripts (ORB, ORD, REV with marks, VAR 03-root-hodge.tex:561-589): device reuse across the model's own work. Pivot distance from L is more than one step (needs choosing S = full period image rather than the line image, plus a new rank-loss lemma with three distinct proofs).
eureka_candidates.against: Every ingredient is named prior art (BC, BBT, Bakker-Tsimerman Ax-Schanuel, Andre normality, BFMT transcendental part, CKS limits, Siu-type volume subtraction); the conclusion is a natural strengthening of BC's 'K_S+D big' and of Viehweg-Zuo / Campana-Paun base-hyperbolicity results; BFMT25 proves semiampleness of the Hodge bundle of Calabi-Yau VHS 'under some extra conditions' - if those conditions hold for root-cover VHS of Kodaira-zero fibres, b-semiampleness would subsume it and the grade drops to N2. Not formalized: cannot be Lean-shortlisted.

correctness_audit.verdict: Extraordinary, unreviewed claims: the family asserts Iitaka's C_{n,m} in full (open since the 1970s; earlier claims by Tsuji 2010 and Maehara 2009 were never accepted, and both are cited as non-inputs), Campana's orbifold Iitaka conjecture, Viehweg's C+_{n,m}, Popa's Conjectures 3.8/3.9 (stratum-smooth form), log Popa-Schnell base nonvanishing, and Kahler b-semiampleness. All five rest on one new Hodge-theoretic statement (adjoint positivity / boundary rank loss) that I could not verify. The deductions AROUND it were checked and are sound at the level read. The Lean certifies only the trivial branch.
checked: ORD 07-ordinary.tex fully: interpolation identity lambda j + (1-lambda) v = 1 and cancellation of -lambda p^*H; A_S ample; period-fibre nonvanishing lemma (cotangent map h_s^*omega_Z -> omega_{W_s} nonzero, KP applied to Y_s -> W_s); effectivity lemma (standard Viehweg flattening argument)
ORB adjoint-addition.tex fully: (1-theta)c + theta a = 1 and (1-theta)eta = theta lambda; p-fibre nonvanishing derived from the perturbed bound
REV reduction.tex fully (all sign cases) and nonvanishing.tex Prop 7.2 / Lemma 7.3 (nef Morse argument correct)
REV geometric-vector.tex read in full; zero-test algebra matches Lean normal_root_zero_test
Elliptic-modular sanity check of adjoint positivity: S=X(1), deg lambda = 1/12, K_S + j lambda big for j>24; boundary drop nu(lambda|cusp)=0<1 holds
Companion locator: REV's 'Foundation Cor 6.2' = ORB applications.tex:173 (root-comparison.tex is a \subsection of Sec. 2, so applications is Sec. 6)
Comparator definitions vs paper (see match_check); trust-surface grep
concerns: Single point of failure: adjoint positivity (ORB Sec. 4 ~920 lines; ORD Secs. 2-5 plus two alternative proofs; REV Secs. 4-5 independent variant with marks). The boundary rank-drop lemma uses Ax-Schanuel, Andre normality and a tangential rank principle near nilpotent and finite-inertia degenerations; read at statement/proof-sketch level only.

If adjoint positivity held this easily, one would expect BFMT's Hodge-theoretic semiampleness machinery to already give C_{n,m}; the papers explain they avoid BFMT Thm 1.5 because it needs effective boundary over the generic point, but do not discuss whether BFMT's purely Hodge-theoretic CY-VHS semiampleness ('under extra conditions') applies to the root-cover VHS. Expert check needed.

Class-C scope (ORB): Lemma 3.3 (adjoint-addition.tex:68-138) applies Fujino's weak positivity 'to this log canonical pair and its projective base' with a Kahler (not projective) source W'; the cited author version treats projective morphisms. The projective corollaries (incl. C_{n,m}) are unaffected, but the Fujiki-class-C generality may need an analytic weak-positivity theorem (e.g. Paun-Takayama) that is not cited there.

Heavy cross-dependence on model-produced companions: REV additivity and VAR main theorem rely on ORB; VAR Cor 1.3 and ORB context rely on the OpenAI log-abundance preprint (itself a claimed proof of log abundance in char 0). An error in ORB/ORD's device propagates to 4 manuscripts (and to families citing them, e.g. 034).

Very dense writing with many 'after further modification / finite level / very general' quantifier switches (e.g. REV's S depends on the section s; y must be fixed before s). I found no error, but these are exactly where gaps hide.
Lean: comparator covers only the kappa(F)=-inf branch; it lacks a Nonempty(FiberModel) clause (harmless weakening). Compile/axiom check not done by this agent.
consistency_checks: ORD and ORB give two different proofs of C_{n,m} (ORD: rational whole-line VHS; ORB: complex character summand, real polarization) and REV re-proves adjoint bigness with its own marked construction rather than citing ORB: internally consistent but not independent (same strategy).
BSA (Sept 10) states it does not use the orbifold theorem; it depends on BFMT25 Thm 1.5 (human, 2025) and MWWWZ25.
